After Rg4+, White can move the king but Black's rook stays on the board and doesn't win material immediately. The pawn move f5+ is clearly superior because it sacrifices the f-pawn to decoy the White king, forcing it to capture on f5, then Black wins the undefended rook on a7.

**Best move:** f5+

**Main line:** f5+ Kxf5 Rxa7 (Black wins the rook)

**Motif:** attraction (or sacrifice with deflection)

**Coaching note for the player:**

When your opponent's piece is undefended and you can't capture it directly, look for checks or forcing moves that bait the king into capturing something, then punish it. Here, f5+ attracts the White king to f5, which frees the a7 rook from defense—you then take it for free. This pattern—sacrifice to lure the king, then win a bigger piece—wins many games at club level.
